title: Magic-Byte Dispatch — Core Method
description: File extensions lie; magic bytes rarely do. The reader inspects the first few bytes of a file — the signatures that identify PDF, ZIP, PNG, and hundreds more — and dispatches to the matching parser. A signature table maps byte patterns to format names, checked longest-first so specific signatures beat generic ones. When no signature matches, the file falls through to text sniffing and finally to the raw reader. Dispatch by content, not by name, is what makes the reader genuinely universal. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.

title: Parser Registry — Core Method
description: Each supported format gets a parser function registered under its format name, with metadata about what it extracts and what it needs. The reader looks up the detected format in the registry and invokes the parser with the file bytes, getting back a uniform document object regardless of source format. New formats are added by writing one function and one registry entry — the core never changes. This plugin design is how a single reader grows to cover hundreds of formats without becoming unmaintainable. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.

title: Structured Text Extraction — Core Method
description: Reading a file usually means extracting its text: walking structured formats and pulling out the human-readable strings in document order. The extractor handles nesting — tables inside sections inside documents — and skips binary blobs that are not text. Extracted text keeps structural hints like headings and list boundaries, because flat text loses meaning. Good extraction is invisible; bad extraction is the garbled output everyone has seen from a broken PDF converter. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.

title: Streaming Reads — Core Method
description: Some files are larger than memory, so the reader streams: it yields records or chunks one at a time while the parser maintains its position. Streaming parsers are written as generators, which keeps the interface identical to batch parsing from the caller's view. Backpressure is natural — the consumer simply stops asking. This is the only sane way to read multi-gigabyte logs, dumps, and archives on ordinary machines. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.

title: Raw Fallback Reader — Core Method
description: When no parser claims a file, the raw fallback reader still returns something useful: the byte length, an entropy estimate, printable-string extraction, and a hexdumps of the head. This guarantees the universal reader never fails outright — worst case, it describes the unknown. Fallback output is clearly labeled as unparsed so downstream tools do not mistake strings for structure. Graceful degradation beats a crash, every time. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.
